courses.name: Reading and Comprehension
courses.summary: Reading for meaning under time pressure: inference, author's purpose, tone, and the close reading the OC and Selective papers are built on.
covers: Inference and drawing conclusions from evidence
Author's purpose, tone and point of view
Vocabulary in context, including unfamiliar words
Cloze and sentence-completion passages
Matching extracts to statements under timed conditions

courses.name: Thinking Skills
courses.summary: The reasoning paper, which is the one most students have never seen before: logic puzzles, sufficient and necessary conditions, pattern and spatial reasoning.
covers: Logical deduction and valid argument
Necessary versus sufficient conditions
Number and pattern reasoning
Spatial reasoning, nets and rotations
Problem solving against the clock

courses.name: Mathematical Reasoning
courses.summary: Worded, multi-step problems rather than drill: the arithmetic is rarely the hard part, and reading the question properly usually is.
covers: Multi-step word problems
Fractions, ratio and proportional reasoning
Measurement, time and money in context
Working backwards and checking an answer is sensible
Showing a method that survives a second look

courses.name: Writing
courses.summary: Narrative and persuasive writing to a brief, marked against the criteria the tests use, with the craft taught rather than assumed.
covers: Narrative: short story, personal recount, description
Persuasive: essay, speech, discussion
Writing to a form: article, letter, diary entry, review
Openings, structure and endings that land
Marked feedback on content, structure, vocabulary, fluency and mechanics

advantages.heading: Why families choose us
advantages.lede: Six things that are hard to find together anywhere else in Sydney.

items.title: Teachers who sat these tests and won
items.body: James Ruse graduates, Mathematics Olympiad medallists and university literature prize shortlistees. The people in front of your child have been through the selective system themselves and teach it from the inside.
page: Every teacher in front of a class here has sat the tests they are teaching. James Ruse graduates, Mathematics Olympiad medallists, and shortlistees for university literature prizes.

That matters for a reason that is easy to miss. A tutor who has only read about the Thinking Skills paper teaches the question types. Somebody who sat it under time, at ten years old, teaches what the paper is actually doing to a child in the room - which question to leave, when a neat-looking answer is a trap, and what to do with eight minutes left and four questions to go.
It also sets the ceiling of the conversation. A child who asks a hard question gets a real answer, not a redirection to the answer key.

items.title: Material you cannot buy anywhere else
items.body: Rich, multi-step questions written by our own teachers. Nothing off the shelf, nothing recycled from the workbooks every other centre hands out.
page: Every question your child sees here was written by one of our teachers, for our classes.

Walk into most centres and the handouts are the same handful of published workbooks, reprinted. Children who have been coached for two years have seen those questions before, which means the practice measures memory rather than reasoning, and a parent paying for a year of it is buying a false reading of where their child stands.

Our questions are multi-step on purpose. A single question will ask a child to extract a fact, hold it, and use it against a second constraint - because that is what the real papers do, and because a question with one move in it cannot tell you anything useful about a strong child.

items.title: The most powerful study platform in NSW
items.body: Homework that marks itself, a revision hall that brings every wrong answer back until it is right three times, guided writing, and a line straight to the teacher when a student is stuck.
page: Classes are once a week. The other six days are where the gap between students actually opens up, so every student here has a portal of their own.

Homework is set by their teacher and marked the moment it is handed in, question by question, with the reasoning shown rather than a letter. Every question a student gets wrong becomes a revision card that comes back days later, and again after that, and is only retired once they have answered it correctly three separate times.

There is guided writing that asks for a plan, reads what has been written and says what is working and what is missing without writing it for them. There is a line straight to their own teacher when they are stuck on a question, and the question comes back to be tried again once it is answered.
And there are reports you can actually read: where your child sits against the cohort, which topics are weak, and what was handed in late.

items.title: A track record over five years
items.body: More than 150 students placed at top-tier selective schools, James Ruse, North Sydney Boys and North Sydney Girls among them.
page: Over the last five years we have placed more than 150 students at top-tier selective schools, James Ruse, North Sydney Boys and North Sydney Girls among them.

We would rather you read that carefully than be impressed by it. A number like that is produced by a cohort over years, not by any single child's term, and nobody can promise your child a place at a particular school. What the record tells you is that the method has been run long enough, on enough students, to know it works on more than the naturally gifted.
If you want to know how children like yours have gone specifically, ask us. We will tell you honestly, including when we think another centre or another year would suit you better.

items.title: In-depth explanations for every question
items.body: Not just the letter of the right answer. Why it is right, why each of the others is tempting, and what to look for the next time a question is built the same way.
page: A wrong answer that is only ever marked wrong teaches a child nothing except that they got it wrong.

Every question in our material carries a worked explanation: why the right answer is right, why each of the wrong answers was built to be tempting, and what to look for the next time a question is put together the same way. The last part is the part that transfers. Children do not improve by learning answers, they improve by learning to recognise the shape of a question.
Those explanations sit in the portal next to the question, so a child working at home on a Tuesday night has the same explanation in front of them that they would get in class.

items.title: Small classes, on purpose
items.body: Focused and intense, with enough room for a teacher to notice what one child in particular has not understood.
page: Our classes are deliberately small, and we hold them that way even when there is a waiting list.

The reason is simple arithmetic. In a room of thirty, a teacher can mark the room's average. In a room of a handful, a teacher notices that one particular child has quietly stopped attempting the second half of the reasoning paper, and can do something about it that week rather than at the end of term.
Small does not mean gentle. The pace is intense and the material is hard, which is the point; a child who is never stretched in the room will be stretched for the first time in the exam hall.
